newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX March heat off sharply on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX March heat off sharply on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil sharpened its declines Friday particulary in the March contract which fell victim to profit-taking after garnering a host of long positions amid a rally in refined products this week.
"All the open interest went to March after shorts covered in Feb ahead of the expiry in both gasoline and heat, so that's where the profits are being taken," said a refined products dealer.
At 1413 EST, March heat was off 1.96 cents a gallon at 66.10 cents after hitting a new session low of 66.00 cents. Feb heat was off 1.54 cents at 68.80 cents a gallon.
The Feb refined products contract expires at market's close Friday. Prompt heat rose 4.10 cents over the last two sessions, but bearish weather forecasts have sparked consolidation.

"The March losses are just massive confirmation that the rally was Feb short covering where the speculators left for March," said a dealer. Gasoline's Feb/March contango evaporated as selling in March gasoline pushed it down 1.30 cents to 68.35 cents while Feb gasoline was off 1.02 cents at 69.80 cents.
March crude was off 56 cents a barrel at $24.31.
Pressure from refined product declines pushed prompt crude through minor support of Thursday's low of $24.43, steepening its losses.
"Crude is selling off with heat which is down on the weather," said a crude dealer.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp saw temperatures moderating to normal next week in the northeastern United States, the largest heating oil market in the world.
"The rally was overdone in heating oil. We are trading the spring months now," noted refined product dealer.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
